notes: Many posts make two moves at once and would need a primary-code rule: the most common overlaps are (a) 'if we stop China wins' combined with insulting the author, (b) marketing-stunt accusations combined with 'AI is just autocomplete', and (c) relay/translation posts that append a one-line fearful exclamation. A large share of high-engagement items are not addressed to the author at all but are arguments between commenters (sceptic vs. rebuttal, China-hawk vs. anti-nationalist), so a reply-target field (author / other replier / general audience) would add resolution the taxonomy lacks. The China/national-security thread is the single densest counter-argument and effectively functions as a sub-debate with its own recurring rebuttals. Non-English posts skew heavily toward relay-plus-emotion and pop-culture framing rather than argument, so language correlates with category and could bias share estimates. Quote tweets skew to amplification, virality metrics and jokes; replies skew to argument, questions and insults. Finally, a noticeable minority of posts are quasi-institutional (politicians announcing legislation, news accounts, safety-org recruiters) rather than ordinary public reaction, and they sit awkwardly inside the same buckets as individual voices.
